title: Uniform log Iitaka fibrations and bounded moduli denominators
main_claim: For d>=5 (the argument works in every dimension) and finite Phi in [0,1]∩Q, there is m(d,Phi) such that for any projective lc pair (X,B) over an algebraically closed field of char 0 with coefficients in Phi, K_X+B Q-Cartier and kappa>=0: V_m(D)≠0 and the section ratios in degree m generate the whole Iitaka field K(D). The key intermediate result (Thm 1.3/thm:moduli-denominator) is a uniform Cartier denominator p(d,Phi) for the moduli b-divisor of the normalized canonical bundle formula. This comes from a uniform weight-denominator theorem q(s,m) for log pluriforms over curves.

issues.location: Prelim Thm 2.1 (normal-index, cite U Thm 1.2), used in Prop 6.1, Lemma 5.6 and the proof of the main theorem
issues.description: The whole result depends on companion inputs. These are U: bounded index for normal lc CY pairs with DCC coefficients in every dimension, which is essentially the open index conjecture; LA: existence of good minimal models / log abundance; and SD: arithmetic Stein-degree bounds. All character bounds for the CY, HK and RC factors (Lemma normal-character), as well as p_0, go through U's theorem. This paper's own reductions to these inputs check out.
issues.evidence: Lemma normal-character reduces the bound on the order of lambda to principalizing a(K+Delta) on A/<gamma> using thm:normal-index with coefficient set Psi_p. When T is smooth, this is exactly the statement that the index conjecture bounds non-symplectic characters on CY manifolds. The family-034 board also notes that U-type statements imply open Betti-number bounds.

issues.location: Lemma marked-semistable together with the paragraph after Cor block-forms
issues.description: Equivariant semistable reduction is only sketched. Semistable reduction needs a further extension of the curve field, after which the inertia lift g and sigma=g^{s!} have to be re-lifted, and the models must be equivariant for the new lift. The paper handles this by saying compatible finite-order lifts extend to composita and that the toroidal subdivision can be made equivariant. This is plausible and standard (KKMS/KNX), but no details are given.
issues.evidence: 'After a finite extension of curve fields and replacement by compatible finite-order lifts of the actions, there are equivariant smooth projective models...'. The argument is a sketch via barycentric subdivision and a citation to [U, Sec 4] and [KNX].

coverage:
I read all 2255 lines of LaTeX. Steps checked in detail:
- Curve MMP lemma: vertical rays come from the length bound with deg A > 2 dim X.
- Weight rules: the base-change factor l comes from ord_E' u = a·ord_E z / l.
- SNC weight lemma: re-derived the log-discrepancy identity.
- Prepared dlt model: E_N is vertical and Q-trivial over C, so E_N = a f^*c, and a = 0 by the infimum.
- Residue reduction: degree bounded by SD with t = 1; the weight scales by e; fibre divisors are lc centres with coefficient 1 in the different.
- RC automorphism lemma: a finite invariant measure plus Poincaré recurrence rules out G_a/G_m; Pic^0 = 0.
- Minimal-RC choice.
- Semilinear block separation: off-diagonal entries of End(T_R) preserving T(-log) vanish via slices; g^{s!} fixes the primitive central idempotents; constant fields of complementary derivations; quasi-étaleness; the graph-fibre-dimension argument for regularity.
- Block forms and their descent.
- Character cancellation: checked the leading-coefficient computation, giving zeta^{b·ord a}·prod lambda^{m/p} = 1 and hence mbQw in Z.
- Abelian character: phi(n) <= C(2h,h), and unipotent factors do not change eigenvalues.
- Equivariant good model: quotient MMP, dlt preservation, exact log-generator equation.
- Other characters: Du Bois base change; holomorphic Lefschetz fixed points (trace 1 for RC, Newton identities for HK, 1+(-1)^h·lambda^{-1} for CY); at most h+1 components through a point; residue character; quotient coefficient set Psi_p is DCC.
- Slice lemma: re-derived ord_E(Omega)/m + 1 = (alpha-1)a_E + 1 - b_E, giving weight = alpha - 1 + t_P.
- Exact presentation: checked the identity n(V - p_0 f^*L) = Div(h^{p_0}·psi^n).
- Moduli denominator: coeff M_W = alpha + t_P - 1 - coeff K_W; nefness on any determination.
- BZ Thm 1.3 setup: E = A - B_W >= 0 exceptional; DCC via HMX ACC for lct.
- Rounded section comparisons, the tensor-independence argument in field descent, and the dlt-modification/MMP reduction.
Not audited: the companion papers U, LA and SD, and the cited MW product theorem, beyond checking that their quoted statements are used within their hypotheses.
sibling_notes: Consistent with family-034 entries for U (rank167), U4/relative (rank187), LA (rank235) and SD-related papers: all no_gap_found, but conditional on the companion chain. In this paper the substantive load is on U Thm 1.2 (lc CY index for DCC coefficients). The rank171 sibling notes that U-type statements would imply bounded b2 for HK manifolds, which is open. The new contributions here (the RC/semilinear block separation, the fixed-point and normal-component character bound, and the slice weight identity) all check out.
